notes.title: Why we donated $2,366.68 USD to charity
notes.content:
So you may have noticed on our store pages we have a little piece of text that says we donate 10% of all of Epiphany City's profits.  Well it took us awhile to decide where to donate the money, but as promised we have done just that, and we've settled on donating the money to specialized adoption coalitions.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/75lysMG.png[/img]

[h3]Why Adoption?[/h3]

There are many places our money could have gone.  In the past we've donated to BLM initiatives (specifically BLM Chicago), feeding the homeless initiatives, and human trafficking prevention among many others.  However after doing some research we've decided that our money would have the highest beneficial impact if we aided the adoption of orphans.

There are many reasons for this, but [b]the bottom line is, almost any problem in society you want to improve can be solved by adoption.[/b] Homelessness, education and drop-out rates, drug and alcohol abuse, crime and prison overcrowding, unemployment, financial instability, illness and mental health, obesity, early mortality, you name it, adoption probably has it covered.

In addition, there are a whole host of debilitating issues that occur in children without loving parents.  Growing up without a father figure increases school drop-out rates by 71%, delinquency and crime by 85%, homelessness by 90%, teen pregnancy increases by 5-8x, drug and alcohol abuse drastically increases, and even 60% of all youth suicides are from fatherless homes.  Of course, growing up WITH attentive parents provides an immeasurable amount of benefit as well, including 55% more likely to enroll in college, 130% more likely to hold leadership positions, and tons more.  I don't need to go into too many details as this is stuff anyone can google themselves, but it is one of the most debilitating circumstances to have to grow up without loving parents.  

[img]https://i.imgur.com/yaufmsi.png[/img]

However, solely providing support for adoption agencies alone results in a whole new host of challenges, as there are unfortunately many families who sign up for adoption or foster care solely to reap extra financial benefits.  So with that in mind, [b]we've donated $2,000 to Foster the City[/b], which is a coalition that works with licensed foster and adoption agencies to both pre-approve and support families that can provide the loving care that orphans need.  We've also donated [b]$366.58[/b] to Berean Community Church which runs its own internal adoption agency that does almost the exact same thing.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/SeNikOs.png[/img]

[b]We chose these two adoption organizations for 3 reasons.[/b]  First, as we said, both are very diligent about which families qualify for adoption, as there are many aspects to consider when finding a proper home for an orphan. Second, our funds are relatively limited, so giving a small(ish) amount to a gigantic corporation may not only barely make a difference in their bottom line, but may also be used less efficiently, as there can be much more red tape to work through and friction/interference from various levels of government. And third, I have personally met with or spoken to people from both organizations, so I have been able to personally scout out and verify the people in charge and how they operate. Foster the City in particular had a base out in the Northern California Bay Area (Foster the Bay), which is where I was located for the majority of Epiphany City's development, so I wanted to aid that location as well.  

Also I shouldn't have to say this, but just in case I do want to note that I am not personally affiliated with either of the organizations or benefit from any of their operations, so it's not like I'm just paying myself in a roundabout way or anything.




Last but not least, [b]Epiphany City is at a limited time discount of 25% off![/b] This is the deepest discount we've had EVER, so if that's what you've been waiting for, now's the time =)


Thank you so much for reading this particular email as it means a lot to me, and I hope you have a wonderful week.
[i]- Dave[/i]

notes.title: How I Used GMTK's Boss Keys To Design My Puzzle Game
notes.content:
[i]Disclaimer: This isn't exactly an announcement about Epiphany City, but rather just a piece I've been wanting to write for a long time and had nowhere else to put it.  Note that this does contain spoilers for Epiphany City- however most of these images were made at the start of development so there have been many changes to each area since then.  Of course, the core concepts remain the same.[/i]



I've been a fan of Mark Brown's Game Maker's Toolkit for over 4 years now.  One of the earliest videos I remember watching was one of his famous Boss Keys videos, where he elegantly laid out the design of each Zelda dungeon.  I was thus inspired to use these learnings in my own indie game, and as a Patreon subscriber I also got access to the icons and layouts that he used in his videos.  So here's the general design sentiment behind each area of Epiphany City.

[url=https://youtu.be/E7sm-0nGV34?t=565][img]https://i.imgur.com/gLF3VoY.png[/img][/url]
[i]^Click here for one example of Mark Brown's Boss Keys series.  You probably want to watch one of these first to understand the graphs in this article.[/i]


[h2]Ocean Dungeon[/h2]

Initially, Epiphany City only had 3 main gameplay areas, which are basically outdoor dungeons.  We wanted them to not only scale in complexity, but offer more freedom and rewards for exploration.  This made sense as not only would the player get more comfortable with the game, but also Lily, our game's protagonist, would improve and grow her world-manipulation powers.

Mark Brown states in his Boss Keys videos that a wider graph suggests more freedom of exploration, as it allows the player to tackle obstacles in almost any order they wish.  On the other hand, a tall and narrow graph suggests linearity- there is no way forward except to get the first key first, then the second key second, and the third key third.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/E2pNhz3.png[/img]

So with this in mind, the first Ocean area starts narrow, and slowly widens.  There is only one way to solve the first section and it requires you to get what you need in a specific order.  But the second section allows the player to equally choose one of two paths to go down, and the third is a complete release of linearity as the player can tackle any piece of the final puzzle in any order.  This not only adds variety as the player progresses, but matches their comfortability with the game and puzzles as they increase in skill.

Full Map here:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/c7CEtmQ.png[/img]

[b][url=https://imgur.com/a/cysYZDK]Click here for a more detailed map breakdown.[/url][/b]

Regardless, the layout of the Ocean is rather simple, and it serves as a good opener for players to explore.


[h2]Sky Mountain[/h2]

Originally named very simply as just "Town", this area adds more complexity into the mix.  Not only does it introduce an evolution of the game's main puzzle mechanic, but splits the map into two sections.  Either section can be completed in either order, and as long as the player reaches the end in both sections they can unlock the final screen.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/miF5oOE.png[/img]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/MMKF8dU.png[/img]

[b][url=https://imgur.com/a/DKutwPY]See a full breakdown of both sections here.[/url][/b]

[h2]Bloom National Park[/h2]

Lastly, we come to the "Park", which is absolutely freeform, with almost no linearity at all.  The player is able to do any screen in basically any order, and can even leave one halfway through to complete another if they so choose.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/M0U0HCR.png[/img]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/l0p6m1b.png[/img]

[b][url=https://imgur.com/a/zZ1ETax]Full breakdown here.[/url][/b]

However, those of you who have played Epiphany City already will know that this isn't quite the same in the final game.  This is due to the fact that early playtesters often got lost, confused, and frustrated as they didn't know where they were supposed to go or what parts of the map led to other parts.  I am positive a better designer than myself could've still made all of this work, but alas, I was young and inexperienced, so I simply gave the area more structure.  And it all seemed to work out anyway, as Bloom National Park is generally regarded as the best area in the game.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/pcjpkQt.png[/img]
[i]Well, tied with Sky Mountain at least.[/i]


Now, we did end up going back and adding one more area, which ended up being the perfect demo / prologue to the main game.  It had all the creative, out-of-the-box puzzles and meta-level surprises that the rest of the game had, but it did so without any confusion or interruptions to flow statedue to its extremely linear design:

[img]https://i.imgur.com/7epV5gw.png[/img]


If you want to experience that for yourself, you can play our Prologue for free here:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1593730/Epiphany_City_Prologue/


So that's how Epiphany City started, almost 4 years ago.  Thanks to all our players, we have tons of ideas on how to improve and evolve our designs, our puzzles, and our "dungeons" if we ever make another game.  So with that, thank you to our players, thank you to Mark Brown, and thanks to yourself for reading this far.  I'll see you in the comments of the next Boss Keys video =P

Sincerely,
- Dave

notes.title: Week 1 Patch Notes & Current Work
notes.content:
Hi.  Thank you all so much for playing or even just being interested in Epiphany City.  There is much more I could say about all the kind words and encouraging reviews we've received, but for now, let's just cut to the chase.

[h2]Future Plans[/h2]

Here are some of our next steps and patch notes we've done since the game came out.

[olist]
[*]Epiphany City's Original Soundtrack will most likely be available in a week.  It is [b]47 tracks[/b], including [b]13 bonus[/b] tracks and will cost [b]$4.99[/b].
[*]Epiphany City is currently being translated to [b]5 out of our 8 priority languages[/b], with more to come.
[*]We plan to add some thematic art to the sides of the screen to replace the black bars.
[*]Working on obtaining the Switch dev kit asap... not sure how much that matters to Steam folk but if you have friends that don't use Steam then you can let them know.
[*]When we start to receive some of the money from Valve we will talk about where our donations will be used.
[/olist]

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]

These are some of the major changes made since launch.  They are not all part of one update, but rather just a log of things that got fixed since the game came out.

[list]
[*]Fixed a bug where you couldn't return to Bloom National Park if you left its first screen.
[*]Fixed a bug where the sides of the screen would turn white after certain cutscenes instead of black
[*]Math puzzles now solve properly even when many objects are moved and reset multiple times
[*]Many adjustments made to the Math puzzles in general
[*]Fixed a bug where framing a security camera and then getting seen by a different one would move the framed camera
[*]Fixed a bug where you couldn't drop the empty frame in a certain spot in the second security camera room
[*]If two camera lights are triggered simultaneously, the game will no longer trigger the 'caught' event twice
[*]The painting in the security camera area now properly resets its rotation upon triggering a camera
[*]An area towards the ending of the game no longer has a completely black screen
[*]Framed objects should appear on a layer above unframed objects more consistently
[*]Not a bug, but deleting or uninstalling vJoy has so far fixed most controller issues.  3Dconnexion was affecting the rest of the controller issues.
[/list]
We are aware of other issues and are working on them alongside our next steps.

___________________

Thank you for reading.  I always thought this was super cliche, but everyone who has played the game really is my hero.  You don't know how much everything has meant to me and how much everything helps us support our families.

Thanks again,
[i]- Dave[/i]

notes.title: Release Notes & Future Roadmap
notes.content:
[h2][b]Epiphany City is OUT NOW!!![/b][/h2]

What are you waiting for?  There is a [b]10% launch discount[/b] available for 1 week, so take advantage of it!  And thank you so much for following us throughout this entire journey <3


However, there's both good news and bad news.  Brace yourselves (I am already bracing myself for the backlash).

[b]#1 - Mac[/b]
[list]
[*] Bad news first.  I know we had a Mac build for the Prologue but for some reason it is only building in 32-bit, which Apple no longer supports.  In order to build a 64-bit build we'd apparently need to transfer all our files to a Mac and build it with the same version of Unity... but we are having trouble finding someone we know with a Mac capable of doing that (aka a Mac that's not a work laptop and not 8+ years old).  Apparently there are some ways to play 32-bit games on a Mac still but I know this isn't ideal.[/list]
[b]TL;DR - Mac build may not be available on release.  I am really, really sorry.[/b]  If anyone has any ideas for how else to get it done, please let us know.

[b]#2 - Controllers[/b]
[list]
[*]Steam input isn't fully integrated, so the control scheme is currently set as follows (the image is of an Xbox controller but it should work for Xbox, PlayStation, and Switch controllers):
[url=https://imgur.com/ZAynzVg][img]https://i.imgur.com/YgjGVrk.png[/img][/url]
[*]Technically you can remap the face buttons of a controller by clicking "Controller Configuration in your library, but you have to remap them to specific keys on the keyboard for it to work.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/LePHZbv.png[/img]
[*]That also means there are only mouse & keyboard button prompts in-game.
[*]We couldn't get joystick controls working for certain parts of the game, so for now only D-pad is enabled to reduce confusion and mid-game switching.
[/list]
[b]#3 - Resolution[/b]
[list]
[*] You can change your resolution, but for now it must be adjusted in the Unity pop-up window before the game starts.
[/list]
[b]#4 - Settings[/b]
[list]
[*]At the moment, you can only access the settings menu by pausing during active gameplay (aka, if you pause during a cutscene you won't be able to access it).  So if you want to adjust volume right away you will have to quit to the main menu.
[/list]
[h1]Post-release roadmap:[/h1]

[b]#1 - Porting.[/b] Our priority of which platforms to port to is in this order:
[olist]
[*] Steam Deck Verified (3 months)
[*] Nintendo Switch (1 year, pending approval)
[*] Xbox Game Pass (unknown)
[/olist]
[b]#2 - Localization.[/b] Translations will heavily depend on how well Epiphany City sells, but if we can afford it we will prioritize these languages:
[list]
[*] Portuguese (Brazil)
[*] Simplified Chinese
[*] Spanish (Spain & Latin America)
[*] German
[*] French
[*] Japanese
[*] Korean
[/list]
This is due to data that showed which countries were most interested in playing Epiphany City.

[b]#3 - Accessibility options.[/b] We would love to add the following if possible:
[list]
[*]An option to change stylized fonts like the Prophecy and Rose's post-it note into a more standard font.
[*]An option to add a font easier to read for people with reading disabilities (something like Open Dyslexic or Dyslexie).
[*]Additional accessibility options for people with motor disabilities.
[*]You can already change your keybinds using the Unity settings window that appears before the game launches, but it would be nicer to have it available in-game.
[*]Same with the screen resolution.
[/list]
[b]#4 - Original Soundtrack[/b] 
[list]
[*]We plan to add the full soundtrack on Steam soon.
[/list]
[b]#5 - DLC[/b] 
[list]
[*]We initially planned to have bonus character backstories and even a post-credits scene that unlocked after completing the game, but we have run out of both time and money so they will need to be added in later. If and when they are added in, they will be included for free.
[/list]

-----------------------------------

I am so excited for you to experience the full game of Epiphany City, and can't wait to see what you all think.  Although no creative work is perfect, I believe Epiphany City accomplishes everything we initially set out to do, and we hope that everyone appreciates it as much as our private playtesters who have completed the full game.

Thank you so much for coming along on this journey with me <3

- Dave

[img]https://i.imgur.com/eoPRYnC.png[/img]

notes.title: Epiphany City officially launches April 12!
notes.content:
[h2]Epiphany City will be released on April 12, 2022, at 5:00am PT (Pacific Time)![/h2]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/bZ8lEtU.png[/img]

Yes!  We finally have an official release date! 
You can use this link to figure out exactly what time this is for you:
[url=https://www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/converter.html?iso=20220412T120000&p1=tz_pt]https://www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/converter.html?iso=20220412T120000&p1=tz_pt[/url]


As much as we wanted to release the game by March (and even though we probably could), we want to take a little extra time to do one last round of QA testing and iron out all the little bugs and things to make sure the game is 100% awesome on release.  Add that to the crazy amount of high profile games coming out in March and we realized it was best to hold off until early April.


You can also check out the [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jDtIyHiOuFQ][b]Official Release Date Trailer[/b][/url] (although you might recognize it if you've been to our Steam page lately).

Thank you so much, we are almost done.
- A very weary yet excited Dave

[img]https://i.imgur.com/HJGZNoI.png[/img]


__________________________________

[h3]For those of you who have been asking how best to support Epiphany City:[/h3]
[i](Don't feel obligated to do these if you don't want to!  This is mostly for close friends and family who have been asking how they can help)[/i]


In order from most important to least important:

[b]#1: Buy Epiphany City the day it releases[/b]
[i]Why: To help us get on Steam's "New and Trending" list[/i]

There will be a discount on release, so please take advantage of that!  Some of you have told me that you'd prefer to buy the game at full price just to help us out, but trust me when I say that buying the game during the launch wave will make a MUCH bigger difference than paying that one extra dollar =P


[b]#2: Leave a review ASAP[/b]
[i]Why: Steam actively hides games with less than 10 reviews[/i]

Even if you're not done with the game yet, you can still write something like "Loving [this part of the game] so far, will update this review when I've beaten the game!" and it will give us a gigantic boost on Steam's algorithm. But don't feel obligated to write a positive review, as either negative or positive reviews help get us toward that 10 review threshhold.


[b]#3: Click Wishlist & Follow[/b]
[i]Why: To help get us on Steam's "Popular Upcoming" list[/i]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/71hvuNF.png[/img]


[b]#4: Tell everyone you know about Epiphany City![/b]
[i]Why: To help with #1-3[/i]

Post about it on your favorite gaming subreddit, send people our trailers, tell your friends to wishlist Epiphany City, and/or have them [url=https://www.epiphanycity.com/demo]sign up for our mailing list[/url]!  Every little bit goes a long way and we never know which actions will become the difference maker in the end.


We can do this! <3
- Sincerely, a very thankful Dave

[img]https://i.imgur.com/clHyVRU.png[/img]

notes.title: New Year Update!
notes.content:
Hey I haven't posted an update in awhile so I thought I'd let you know what everyone's been up to since the new year:
 

[list]
[*] [b]Art:[/b] Currently getting the VERY last batches of art assets done.  We brought a handful of extra artists on board to help us get these done in time, so theoretically we'll have everything completed by the end of the month!
[*] [b]Music:[/b] Romeo's developing Lily's Main Theme and adding all the leitmotif variations for every scene it'll play its part in.
[*] [b]Programming:[/b] Cameron is currently filling out the supplementary things, like the pause menu, volume options, saving and loading, controller support, achievements, and everything else in-between.
[*] [b]Design & Writing:[/b] As of Dec 29th, 2021, the entire game has been playable from start to finish!  Which has been super fun.  Technically we had a full build awhile ago, but it was super sketchy and unfinished and full of temporary "Google Image" assets that ended up being taken out.  But right now the game actually looks pretty good!
[/list]

However, there's still a ton of work left.  Once we've got every single asset we need in the game, we'll take the entire month of February to polish everything up (it takes a lot longer than you'd think).  Every little animation, sound, visual effect, word of dialogue, timing of appearances, etc will need to be tweaked so that every part of the game is up to the level of polish that the Prologue had.
 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/0r6tWtU.gif[/img]
[i](This little pond animation is just one example of all the stuff we have to add)
[/i]

That having been said, progress has honestly been going much better than I expected.  Implementing a lot of the auxiliary stuff on the programming side has been going really smoothly (so far), so hopefully that means we'll actually be done by [b]MARCH 2022[/b].


So yeah, that's honestly it!  Thanks so much for reading and following along on this journey... I know I've said that multiple times now, but that's because I really actually mean it!  

You're the best,
[i]- Dave[/i]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/ZRe2XvQ.png[/img]

notes.title: Closed Beta Results & Infographic!
notes.content:
Hi Steam Community!  We just ran our first Closed Beta.  If you missed it, [b]you can still download the demo AND sign up for the next one at [url=https://www.epiphanycity.com/demo]epiphanycity.com/demo[/url].[/b]

This post is long enough to warrant its own Table of Contents.  So buckle up, here's what we got:

[olist]
[*] Infographic
[*] Roadmap of Development (including our next Beta test!)
[*] Some Unfortunate News
[/olist]

[h2]Infographic + Survey Results[/h2]

In general, most people enjoyed the puzzles, story, art, dialogue, music, and characters.  Which kinda sounds like everything?  Except there were tons of technical complaints, like the clunky grid-based movement, lack of volume sliders, no "Quit" button on the title screen, etc.  But for now, we are more than happy that we hit all the big stuff, and will continue to work on those smaller technical fixes... although you might want to read the last section of this post.

[url=https://i.imgur.com/CnyR7nI.png][img]https://i.imgur.com/CnyR7nI.png[/img][/url]


[h2]Development Roadmap[/h2]
Epiphany City is roughly split into 8 sections:

[olist]
[*] Intro / Opening Scenes
[*] Museum (aka what you played in the Prologue)
[*] Yellow Fields + Ocean Beach
[*] Town Gate + Sky Mountain
[*] Mischief Managed
[*] Bloom National Park
[*] Dark Forest
[*] Ending
[/olist]

The next playtest will include [b]sections 3-6[/b].  If you do not want any of the game spoiled, I recommend holding off on this test because this is the meat of the game and therefore the majority of the gameplay.  While we expect to have this ready by the [b]end of June[/b], we've pretty much never been perfectly on time with our deadlines so it's probably going to be a bit later than that.

We also plan to test and iterate on the final areas of the game, so if you're an exceptionally brave soul that doesn't mind seeing an ending-in-progress, this might just be your moment.


[h2]Some Unfortunate News and My Apologies
[/h2]So if you haven't looked through the infographic already, one of the biggest complaints (in fact, the biggest complaint by far) was that the movement was too clunky. 

The main issue here is that there is no input buffering on the movement.  This means that you can't input any button commands until Lily has fully reached the next tile she's moving to.  There are many, many more ways to improve a game's movement, but this is the big one.

Unfortunately at this point in development, it's extremely unlikely that we'll be able to add that in, for the following reasons:

[olist]
[*] We were complete noobs when we first started working on Epiphany City (just finished computer science degree, first game ever, never used Unity before, etc).
[*] All of the groundwork/framework for Epiphany City was done when we were complete noobs.
[*] I personally told our programmer to hack together the fastest prototypes he could make, because we wanted the fastest "iterate > test > iterate > test" cycle possible (as this is generally the best way to make a good game)
[*] We always planned to go back and fix the movement, but since Epiphany City has zero need for quick reflexes or precise movement, we kept pushing it back and eventually the project got too big for us to completely start over (currently at ~50,000 lines of code and wishing we could travel back in time and yell our younger selves)
[*] I feel especially bad for this because more than anything, we want to be the developers who listen to their fans and do everything they can to help them enjoy the game. Now of course we wouldn't have gone to such lengths to ask for your brutally honest feedback if we didn't plan on updating and improving the game, but still I felt the need to be upfront about this earlier rather than later.
[/olist]

So TL;DR, I am very sorry, please forgive our team, I promise your feedback is super valuable and we will improve all the other stuff you asked for, but this one thing would require us to remake the entire game so we might not be able to do it.

___________


To close this out, I'll leave you all with a quote from an email that really gave me hope and made my day:


[i]David,
I can’t leave a steam review yet, since the prologue isn’t officially out, so I’ll leave what I would have posted in this email for now.

I was initially put off by the simplistic look of the game—how it played, the character designs/art style. I wouldn't have even considered looking more closely at this game if not for knowing who was involved in its creation. However I was genuinely very impressed by the quality of the puzzles. The dialogue is lighthearted and silly but the story looks like it will take its themes a little seriously. The music is beautiful and a joy to listen to. It honestly looks like a wonderful little game. I'm excited to play more when the game fully releases.

~ [Name hidden for privacy]
Retired Smash Competitor
[/i]


If you made it all the way to the end, you're a true fan and our team couldn't be more blessed to have you with us.  I'm glad that this is interesting enough and I'll work hard so that you can enjoy Epiphany City as soon as possible.

Thanks for reading,
- Dave

notes.title: So What Do You Actually DO in Epiphany City?
notes.content:
Yo what up.  If there was anything about Epiphany City's gameplay that confused you, this should clear everything up!  If not, you can always leave a comment and I'll get back to you.



[h2]1. Find all of the Prophecy's Flowers[/h2]
Lily and Superb Man witness a vision of their world in ruins, and are tasked with finding three mysterious Flowers to fulfill the Sacred Prophecy.  Each Flower will increase the Hero of the Prophecy's powers, until they are strong enough to defeat the evil forces threatening the world and change the future.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/HNZqZlv.gif[/img]


[h2]2. Use magical picture frames to manipulate the world[/h2]
Use Lily's unique powers (that she stole from Superb Man) to manipulate the world and progress through the game.  These include moving things around and even re-contextualizing objects.  Anything is possible, as long as you're imaginative enough!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/t79bt98.gif[/img]


In addition to our creative puzzle mechanics, you'll also go through some more traditional puzzles, like the Spring Flowers from the Ocean, the Blooming Flowers from Sky Mountain, and the Numerical Flowers from Blossom National Park.  I won't spoil how these work- you'll have to figure that out for yourself!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/76bZxZX.png[/img]
(^ Spring Flower puzzles)


[h2]3. Take a break and grab a snack[/h2]
Epiphany City has no time limits, no fast reactions necessary, no fiddling with controls or getting used to foreign physics.  Both Cameron (our programmer) and I have re-designed the game many times over to ensure you just get to enjoy playing the game.  So take your time and enjoy the experience! 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/pRlTGys.gif[/img]
[i]If you're really clever, you can just use your magical frame powers to give yourself more time =P[/i]

There is actually one exception to the fast reactions thing, but I promise you'll be able to get through it no problem, so don't worry.


[h2]4. Eat your snack as you watch the story unfold[/h2]
Once you reach certain milestones, you'll uncover more knowledge and secrets about the world, as well as see more of our major characters in action!  I'll be sending you more blurbs about each of them as well, so keep an eye out for that!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Hf19FSr.gif[/img]

_______

And that's it!  Epiphany City is pretty unique, so there isn't really a game similar to it that helps everyone understand what it's like.  I hope I cleared up a lot of stuff for you all, but now I have two questions for you:

What did you most want to know about Epiphany City before reading this email?  Or is there anything else you're still wondering?
What other games does Epiphany City remind you of?

Don't hesitate to leave a comment and let me know!  It'll help both of us out a lot and I'm always excited to chat.
[i]- Dave[/i]

notes.title: Why We Give Away 10% of Our Profits
notes.content:
Hey everyone, David Elliot here as always.  If you want to get more content like this that isn't on Steam, including fun little character bios and wallpapers and such, [url=https://www.epiphanycity.com/home/#TeamEpiphany]sign up[/url] for our members-only mailing list on our website.


There are 3 things that make us stand out, compared to other studios.

[h2]#1. Our 3 core members were ex-esports pros[/h2]

This is particularly weird when you think about this wholesome, story-driven puzzle game with no fast reactions or complex button inputs necessary, but hey, sometimes you just yearn for that feeling of adventure, that feeling of magic and discovery that you had when you first played an epic video game as a kid.

We were all ranked Top 10 in Southern California for Super Smash Bros Melee at some point in time.  I personally hosted esports events, organized tournaments for some of the most high profile invitationals on Twitch, and have a YouTube channel dedicated to teaching players how to improve at the game.  Those were fun times... but honestly, after all those years of stressful competition, I'm super glad I get to work on a more creative endeavor.


[h2]#2. We're diverse AF[/h2]

This isn't necessarily unique to us only, but if you're familiar with the game dev demographic you know this isn't how things usually go.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/PLRdaVl.png[/img]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/oGEW6X0.png[/img]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/b4GS1Zy.png[/img]

As you can see, about 70% of the game dev community is a 35 year old white male.  Got nothin' against 35 year old white males, I love 'em, tons of my friends are white males.  Just sayin', our studio happens to have people who are Iranian, Thai, Puerto Rican, Singaporean, Korean, non-binary, and an even 50-50 split of women and men.  And we all work remote, some even from Singapore.  So it's just not your typical development studio.

But anyway, these graphs got me a bit skeptical tbh.  It surveyed people from ages 18-67 but the second graph says there aren't even people younger than 25 in game dev, which would mean half of our studio doesn't even exist. So go figure.


[h2]#3. We give away 10% of our profits to charity[/h2]

This is something that I personally have been doing for the past 8 years.  Anyone who's played the beta version of our demo has read this in our "About the Team" section, but basically, our 3 core, degenerate members (all the esports pros) have received so much good fortune and support in life, that it would be irresponsible not to pay some of it forward.  

Depending on how well Epiphany City does, we may actually give away more than 10%... but we'll see.  



Okay that's all for now.  You can always let me know what you think of these updates, or just talk to me about whatever you want honestly.  Thanks for reading!
[i]- Dave[/i]

notes.title: FAQ (part 1)
notes.content:
Hey everyone, David Elliot here as always.  Before we get to the FAQ, I just wanted to tell you that our [url=http://www.EpiphanyCity.com]official website[/url] is finally public!  You can read more about the game there, and any of your friends who don't use Steam can get notified of sales discounts, original design documents, exclusive wallpapers, soundtracks, and a lot more by joining our [url=http://www.epiphanycity.com/home/#TeamEpiphany]insider group[/url] there.

So with that out of the way, here are some common questions people ask us, and their answers!


[url=https://i.imgur.com/PJBB5JZ.gif][img]https://i.imgur.com/auSUf0P.gif[/img][/url]
[h3]How long is Epiphany City?[/h3]
Current playtests clock in at about 4-5 hours.  Experienced puzzle game fanatics might complete the game sooner.

[h3]How much is it going to cost?[/h3]
Somewhere around $15-$20, but it hasn't been confirmed yet.

[h3]When is it coming out?[/h3]
You know, every time I say the game is almost done I end up being completely wrong, so we're going to wait until we're 100% certain to announce a release date.  However, we currently think we will finish it by Winter 2021.

[h3]How difficult are the puzzles in Epiphany City?[/h3]
Epiphany City is not meant to be super challenging.  As much as we were inspired by games like Braid, The Witness, and even Stephen’s Sausage Roll, the game’s difficulty is a lot closer to something like Paper Mario.  We wanted to make something that would allow non-gamers to see how amazing video games could really be.

[h3]Can I stream your game?[/h3]
Yes, absolutely!  We would especially love it if you streamed our demo, which you’ll be able to download for free soon.  To get notified when the demo goes live, join our [url=http://www.epiphanycity.com/home/#TeamEpiphany]insider group[/url].

[h3]Are there multiple endings?[/h3]
Epiphany City is a mostly linear adventure.  We actually tried to make it open world at first, but failed miserably.  Maybe in our next project we can realize that dream now that we’ve learned so much more about game development.

[h3]Will the game come to [i][insert platform here][/i]?[/h3]
We really want to bring the game to iOS and the Nintendo Switch (if Nintendo accepts us), as those platforms probably fit our game’s vibe the best, but it will probably take an extra year of development at least.



Hey, if you made it to the bottom of this post, you have my thanks, and I'll answer any other questions you have.  Right below this post, there's a button that says "Discuss".  Click it, and reply with one question that wasn't answered here, and I'll get back to you with your answer =)  

Thanks for reading!
[i]- Dave[/i]

notes.title: How It Started >> How It's Going
notes.content:
Our art used to be so bad, that when I first sent my programmer this screenshot...

[img]https://i.imgur.com/YodjTZY.png[/img]

...believe it or not, he said, "That's for our game?  Wow, that looks nice!"




Over the years we've had to update our game's art [b]4 times[/b].  Some areas took more iterations than others, but here is one example of how the background art progressed over the past 3 years.

[h3]Art 1 - Wireframes[/h3]
I was originally raised in UX Design, so to communicate my ideas to artists (and the whole team, really) I created wireframes. 

[url=https://i.imgur.com/YWKkagT.png][img]https://i.imgur.com/ZE8sAkX.png[/img][/url]


[h3]Art 2 - Temp Assets[/h3]
We used temporary assets from other games, as well as my own incredible ability to color in rectangles, to create an area that looked decent enough for a playtester to go through.  Game design is often best done as an iterative process, so the faster we could get a quick 'n' dirty prototype out, the sooner we could start improving on all of our designs.

[url=https://i.imgur.com/6hw7THx.png][img]https://i.imgur.com/RyGKpBb.png[/img][/url]
[i]Bonus points for you if you know where some of these assets are from[/i]


[h3]Art 3 - Orissa Jenkins[/h3]
We've hired over 8 artists over the course of development, but Orissa was one of the few that worked on this area specifically.  I personally made a lot of mistakes and had a lot to learn- where to look for artists, what to look FOR, how to communicate my ideas to them, the formatting and layering of each asset, etc.  Orissa is a fantastic artist (as you can see on her [url=https://www.orissajenkins.com]website[/url]), and neither my mistakes nor the way Steam imports images shows off her true skill.  However, in the end we went with another team.

[url=https://i.imgur.com/KZ6O2lu.png][img]https://i.imgur.com/jTCQ1LJ.png[/img][/url]
[i]Click on any of these images for a higher-res version.[/i]


[h3]Art 4 - Adorabelle & Cindy[/h3]
If you've read our "[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1508530/view/3066359753964559327]About the Team[/url]" post, Adorabelle & Cindy are a team of artists that work together under the moniker "Wanderfaire".  They're incredibly versatile, and I knew I could rely on them because we had worked together before on another game project, where they created a gorgeous-looking world map for a tactical RPG.

[url=https://i.imgur.com/MMufkuO.png][img]https://i.imgur.com/8L6xRtV.png[/img][/url]
[i]The world map for project Super Planet Darkness.  Hopefully I'll get a chance to finish this game one day.[/i]


Not only were they just absurdly skilled artists- but the way they communicated their thoughts, goals, and processes helped me improve in those areas as well.  And so, to cut a long story short, they were amazing, I got better, and they produced some of the prettiest backgrounds for our game- even better than I ever could have hoped for.

[url=https://i.imgur.com/jYgDHaK.png][img]https://i.imgur.com/05NU3rA.png[/img][/url]
[i]The automatic doors slide open. It's sick.[/i]



That's all for today.  We'll be posting more about other screens, character art design, 'dungeon' design, puzzles, story, you name it.  So stay tuned, and thanks for reading!

[i]- Dave[/i]

notes.title: About the TEAM
notes.content:
We'll go into more detail about each person later on, but this will suffice for now.  If you have any questions (either for us or about the game), there's a Discussion post in the Community Hub where you can ask us anything!



[img]https://i.imgur.com/zFGNVPG.png[/img]
[h3][b]David Elliot[/b][/h3]
[h3][i]Creative Director[/i][/h3]
Whether it's game design, writing, business, management, recruiting, marketing, research, or anything else a small business requires, Dave is just daft enough to think he knows what he's doing.  But that's what made this game happen!  If the world was full of superheroes, Dave's power would be "naive optimism", although he probably wishes he got telekinesis instead.


[img]https://i.imgur.com/mGUL7d0.png[/img]
[h3][b]Cameron Ladjevardi[/b][/h3]
[h3][i]Lead Programmer[/i][/h3]
Actually, he's our only programmer.  What a beast.  If he quit we all would have starved.  He loves playing obscure competitive games that have completely died out, and always picks the ugliest character on the entire roster.  But he also holds world records, so he can do whatever he wants, I guess.


[img]https://i.imgur.com/gmPk2GE.png[/img]
[h3][b]KK Hong[/b]
[i]Character Art & Animation[/i][/h3]
Truth be told, KK has drawn probably 70% of the game's assets (including non-character assets), and the game's overall art style was established by him.  Like a Fallout character who's maxed out their "Work Ethic" stat, KK drew all this [i]while also[/i] holding down multiple other jobs and starting his own projects.


[img]https://i.imgur.com/KMGqJTP.png[/img][img]https://i.imgur.com/IZIU4wC.png[/img]
[h3][b]Adorabelle Tan & Cindy Chuang[/b]
[i]Background & Environmental Art[/i][/h3]
While looking for artists to make an RPG world map, Dave found Adorabelle & Cindy on a message board of all places.  Hailing from Singapore, this pair made all of our wildest imaginations come true.  In fact, their drawings ended up [i]better[/i] than what we'd imagined in our heads.  Makes me wonder what goes on in [i]their[/i] heads...


[img]https://i.imgur.com/g1tuJ3D.png[/img]
[h3][b]Romeo Castillo[/b]
[i]Music & Composition[/i][/h3]
Romeo is an extremely fun dude to be around and parties would be super boring without him and his music.  Surprisingly, although Epiphany City's soundtrack is entirely orchestrated, his genres of choice are actually synthwave and chiptune.  Romeo also gets good at video games prodigiously fast, but don't give him any drinks...


[img]https://i.imgur.com/GeL2LY5.png[/img]
[h3][b]Ellie Johnson[/b]
[i]Background, Character, & Various Art[/i][/h3]
On small dev teams, everyone gets really good at doing everything, and Ellie is definitely good at everything.  Without her every section of the game would be like a loading screen forever stuck at 99%, except she also made most of the Museum and National Park areas by herself, so I guess those would be stuck at 1%.  She also has the best taste in movies & shows... but don't tell any of the other members I said that!


Keep an eye out for our next posts about [b]how we designed each area[/b] and the [b]progression of art[/b], where you'll get a better idea of what each person did specifically!  Thanks for reading!  You guys are awesome.
